title: Dialpad vs Loom: Cloud business calling or asynchronous screen-and-camera video?
description: A practical decision guide for teams weighing Dialpad against Loom. They serve different primary jobs: Dialpad focuses on cloud business calling, while Loom focuses on asynchronous screen-and-camera video. Use the workflow criteria below to decide whether you need one, the other, or both; verify current vendor capabilities, terms, and pricing before committing.

features.name: Core task
features.tool1Detail: Evaluate Dialpad when calls, call handling, and phone-based support or sales workflows are central; verify transcription, call routing, and retention controls.
features.tool2Detail: Evaluate Loom when short recorded explanations, demos, and async updates can replace repeat meetings; test recording, captions, sharing permissions, and retention.

features.name: Selection test
features.tool1: Run Dialpad through one representative task and document the result, setup effort, and any gaps.
features.tool1Detail: Confirm the requirements Dialpad must satisfy before evaluating plans or switching tools.
features.tool2: Run Loom through the same decision process.
features.tool2Detail: Check whether Loom solves the same requirement or a separate one.

features.name: Operational checks
features.tool1: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and the ongoing owner for this workflow.
features.tool1Detail: Use vendor documentation and a small pilot; do not infer capabilities from a rating or a generic feature checklist.
features.tool2: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and the ongoing owner for this workflow.
features.tool2Detail: Estimate total cost from the plan and usage you actually need, not an unverified headline price.

features.name: Relationship
features.tool1: Live phone conversations versus recorded async explanations
features.tool1Detail: Do not treat either product as a universal winner; compare it against the job it is meant to do.
features.tool2: Live phone conversations versus recorded async explanations
features.tool2Detail: If the responsibilities are distinct, using both may make sense; confirm the handoff and avoid paying twice for the same capability.

verdict: There is no evidence-based universal winner between Dialpad and Loom because their primary jobs differ. Choose Dialpad if the need described above matches your workflow; choose Loom if its job is the one you need to solve. If both needs exist, assess whether the tools complement each other and define ownership at the handoff. Pilot the relevant workflow, verify current features and plan limits with each vendor, and compare total cost, integrations, privacy, permissions, and support before buying.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Dialpad and Loom?
faqs.answer: Dialpad is used for cloud business calling, while Loom is used for asynchronous screen-and-camera video. Start with the job your team needs to complete rather than comparing them as interchangeable products.

faqs.question: Can Dialpad replace Loom?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. A replacement only makes sense if Dialpad demonstrably covers the requirements you currently rely on Loom for. Test the real workflow and confirm any missing integrations, controls, or outputs before switching.

faqs.question: Can a team use Dialpad and Loom together?
faqs.answer: Potentially, when the team needs both cloud business calling and asynchronous screen-and-camera video. Define which tool owns each step, how information moves between them, and who maintains access and data quality.

faqs.question: How should I compare their costs?
faqs.answer: Check each vendor's current pricing and plan limits, then estimate the total cost for the seats, usage, integrations, support, and administration your workflow requires. Do not rely on stale prices or unverified rating claims.

faqs.question: What is the safest way to choose?
faqs.answer: Write down the must-have outcomes, run a small pilot using the same representative scenario, check security and privacy requirements, and score the results against those outcomes. Keep human review for important decisions and verify vendor claims directly.
